# Picture color-change controls

Original XML/PNG swatches generated by tools/picture_color_change_fixture.py
from this repository's original picture-duotone control. No corpus artwork is
included. Dependencies are Python stdlib, Pillow (HPND), and lxml (BSD).

Twenty-three rows of 32 RGBA swatches cover colors near white and a colored key,
partial/zero source alpha, useA defaults/false/true, replacement alpha, repeated
color changes, and combinations with grayscale, duotone, luminance and picture
alpha. A blue-gray paragraph background exposes transparency. The reference application
exported native.pdf; native-page1.png uses PDFium at 96 DPI. The recorder samples
swatch interiors at 288 DPI and records source/PDF hashes. All native/browser
control rows were visually inspected. Label typography is not the tested subject.

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 20.1.8.16, .17 and .19 define clrChange, clrFrom and
clrTo; CT_ColorChangeEffect defaults useA to true. These controls establish
native reference behavior beyond literal exact color replacement:

- True/default useA matches each decoded RGBA channel within one byte, including
  alpha; two-byte differences do not match. Matched pixels use replacement RGBA.
- False useA ignores declared source/target alpha and matches exact opaque RGB.
  Partial source pixels and neighboring opaque colors remain unchanged.
- Color changes run in source order relative to one another, before grayscale,
  duotone, luminance and the picture-wide alpha modifier, regardless of the
  surrounding XML order. Opposite repeated color-change orders differ.
- Fully transparent source pixels decode to transparent black. A transparent
  black key reveals them; a transparent colored key does not.

Production import validates containers, colors and boolean attributes. The pixel
pipeline implements this compatibility behavior; original drawing XML survives
edits. Generated drawings serialize the resolved effect colors and alpha.

Unit tests compare opaque replacement-only results exactly with native samples.
Combinations allow one byte of existing grayscale rounding difference; partial
alpha composites allow up to five bytes for native/browser premultiplication.
Browser coverage samples all 736 swatches before editing, after editing and after
reopening, checks undo/media preservation, and validates native reference hashes.
These tolerances are explicit limitations, not a pixel-perfect certification.
